symptom: PC in VLAN 30 cannot reach the server, but gateway ping works.
show_command_output: show access-lists: 'deny ip 192.168.30.0 0.0.0.255 any' present in ACL 101 applied inbound on Gi0/1; show ip route: 192.168.40.0/24 via R1 present; show vlan brief: VLAN 30 active, Fa0/2
expected_fault: ACL is blocking traffic from VLAN 30

symptom: PC in VLAN 20 cannot reach any device outside its own VLAN, including the gateway.
show_command_output: show vlan brief: Fa0/3 assigned to VLAN 20 (correct); show interfaces trunk: SW1-SW2 trunk allowed vlans 1,10 (VLAN 20 missing from allowed list)
expected_fault: Trunk link does not allow VLAN 20, so inter-switch traffic for that VLAN is dropped

symptom: PC3 cannot ping its own default gateway.
show_command_output: show ip interface brief on PC3: IP 192.168.10.5, Gateway configured as 192.168.10.254 (does not match R1's actual interface IP 192.168.10.1)
expected_fault: Incorrect default gateway configured on the PC

symptom: All hosts on VLAN 10 lost connectivity to the rest of the network at the same time.
show_command_output: show ip interface brief on R1: GigabitEthernet0/0 status administratively down, protocol down; router-on-a-stick subinterface GigabitEthernet0/0.10 cannot operate while its parent physical interface is down
expected_fault: The parent router interface GigabitEthernet0/0 is administratively shut down, taking down the VLAN 10 subinterface

symptom: New PCs joining VLAN 30 are not receiving an IP address via DHCP.
show_command_output: show ip dhcp pool VLAN30: Total addresses 10, Leased addresses 10, Available 0
expected_fault: DHCP pool for VLAN 30 is exhausted

symptom: PCs in VLAN 40 receive an APIPA address (169.254.x.x) instead of a real IP.
show_command_output: show run | section dhcp: ip dhcp pool VLAN40 configured with network 192.168.50.0 255.255.255.0, but VLAN40 SVI is 192.168.60.1/24 (pool subnet mismatch)
expected_fault: DHCP pool network does not match the VLAN's actual subnet

symptom: PC can ping the server by IP address but cannot reach it by hostname.
show_command_output: show ip interface brief on PC: DNS server configured as 8.8.4.8 (unreachable, typo); ping 8.8.4.8 request timed out
expected_fault: PC is configured with an incorrect/unreachable DNS server address

symptom: Name resolution fails for all clients in the branch office, though the DNS server address is correct.
show_command_output: show ip route on R1: no route to 10.0.0.53/32 (DNS server subnet); ping 10.0.0.53 from R1 fails
expected_fault: No route exists to the DNS server's network

symptom: Branch office (VLAN 50) cannot reach HQ server subnet, everything else within the branch works.
show_command_output: show ip route on R1: no entry for 172.16.0.0/24 (HQ subnet); no static or dynamic route configured toward R2
expected_fault: Missing static/dynamic route to the HQ subnet

symptom: Traffic to the HQ server subnet times out intermittently and traceroute shows it looping between two routers.
show_command_output: show ip route on R2: static route 172.16.0.0/24 via R1 (should be via R3); show ip route on R1: static route back via R2 for same network
expected_fault: Static route configured with the wrong next-hop, creating a routing loop

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi users can reach the internal file server, which should not be allowed.
show_command_output: show access-lists GUEST_ISOLATION: ACL has no deny entry for internal server subnet; show vlan brief: guest SSID mapped to VLAN 1 instead of dedicated guest VLAN
expected_fault: Guest traffic is not isolated - VLAN mapping and ACL rules for guest isolation are missing

symptom: An ACL intended to block Telnet to the router is not working; Telnet still succeeds.
show_command_output: show access-lists 105: 'deny tcp any any eq 23' present but show run | section line vty shows 'access-class' not applied to vty 0 4
expected_fault: ACL exists but is not applied to the vty lines

symptom: An ACL meant to permit only 192.168.1.0/24 is blocking legitimate hosts in that subnet.
show_command_output: show access-lists 110: 'permit ip 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.15 any' (wildcard mask too restrictive, only covers .0-.15)
expected_fault: Incorrect wildcard mask in ACL limits the permitted range

symptom: Internal hosts cannot access the internet even though routing to the ISP looks correct.
show_command_output: show ip nat translations: empty; show run | section nat: 'ip nat inside'/'ip nat outside' not applied to any interface
expected_fault: NAT is not configured on the inside/outside interfaces

symptom: Internet access works for some hosts but new sessions start failing during peak hours.
show_command_output: show ip nat statistics: pool addresses exhausted; show ip nat pool: pool has only 2 public addresses for 50 hosts; no NAT overload/PAT configuration is present
expected_fault: Dynamic NAT pool is too small for the number of hosts and NAT overload is not configured

symptom: A specific port on SW1 shows no link light and the connected PC has no connectivity.
show_command_output: show interfaces Fa0/5: Fa0/5 is administratively down, line protocol is down
expected_fault: Switch port is administratively shut down

symptom: File transfers on a link are extremely slow and show many collisions/errors.
show_command_output: show interfaces Fa0/6: 100Mb/s, half-duplex; show interfaces Fa0/1 on SW2: 100Mb/s, full-duplex
expected_fault: Duplex mismatch between the two connected interfaces

symptom: PC can ping its own gateway but cannot reach any other host on the same subnet.
show_command_output: show ip interface brief on PC: subnet mask 255.255.255.252 (/30) instead of 255.255.255.0 (/24), splitting the subnet incorrectly
expected_fault: Incorrect subnet mask configured on the PC

symptom: Two PCs on the network intermittently lose connectivity and event logs show IP conflict warnings.
topology: PC4 and PC5 on same VLAN
show_command_output: show arp on SW1: 192.168.1.50 mapped to two different MAC addresses at different times
expected_fault: Duplicate/overlapping static IP address assigned to two hosts

symptom: A redundant switch link is unexpectedly unused; all traffic goes over a single path and that link is congested.
show_command_output: show spanning-tree vlan 10: one trunk port role is 'Blocking' as expected by STP, but the active link is the lower-bandwidth 100Mb link instead of the 1Gb link (port cost not tuned)
expected_fault: Spanning Tree port cost is not tuned, so STP is not selecting the higher-bandwidth link as forwarding

symptom: Voice VLAN traffic on a trunk is being tagged incorrectly and phones cannot register.
show_command_output: show interfaces trunk: SW1 native VLAN 1, SW2 native VLAN 99 on the same trunk link; %CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH logged
expected_fault: Native VLAN mismatch on the trunk link

symptom: Employees cannot see the corporate Wi-Fi network in their device's Wi-Fi list.
show_command_output: show run | section wlan: SSID 'Corp-WiFi' configured with 'no broadcast-ssid' (hidden network) though users expect it to be visible
expected_fault: SSID broadcast is disabled, hiding the network

symptom: Devices see the Wi-Fi network but fail to connect, reporting an authentication error.
show_command_output: show run | section wlan: pre-shared key configured as 'Cisco123' but the documented/distributed password is 'Cisco1234' (mismatch)
expected_fault: Incorrect pre-shared key configured on the access point

symptom: Wi-Fi connection is unstable with frequent drops in an office with multiple nearby networks.
show_command_output: show wlan statistics: AP1 and AP2 both configured on channel 6 (overlapping), high co-channel interference reported
expected_fault: Channel overlap/interference between nearby access points

symptom: Hosts in VLAN 60 cannot reach any other VLAN even though the router-on-a-stick is configured.
show_command_output: show run | section Gi0/0: Gi0/0.60 encapsulation dot1Q 60, ip address 192.168.60.254/24 -- but 'show vlan brief' shows Fa0/4 (VLAN60 host port) missing from VLAN60, still in default VLAN 1
expected_fault: Access port for the VLAN 60 host was never assigned to VLAN 60

symptom: During a router failover test, hosts lose their default gateway for about a minute instead of failing over instantly.
show_command_output: show standby brief: R1 priority 100 (default), R2 priority 100 (default), preempt disabled on both -- failover relies on hello/hold timers only
expected_fault: HSRP priorities and preempt are not configured for fast, predictable failover

symptom: A PC's switch port goes into err-disabled state shortly after being connected.
show_command_output: show port-security interface Fa0/8: Port Security enabled, Violation Mode: Shutdown, Maximum MAC 1, Security Violation Count 1; show interfaces Fa0/8 status: err-disabled
expected_fault: Port security violation (maximum MAC address count exceeded) shut the port down

symptom: An ACL meant to restrict traffic leaving the LAN is instead blocking traffic destined to the LAN from outside.
show_command_output: show run | interface Gi0/1: 'ip access-group 120 in' (ACL 120 was written to filter outbound LAN traffic but applied inbound on the WAN interface)
expected_fault: ACL is applied to the wrong interface/direction

symptom: Administrators cannot reach the management IP of SW1 from other VLANs, though the switch itself forwards traffic fine.
show_command_output: show ip interface brief on SW1: Vlan1 up/up, IP address 192.168.1.2, but no default gateway configured ('show ip default-gateway' returns none)
expected_fault: Switch is missing a default gateway for its management VLAN interface

symptom: Users can resolve DNS names correctly, but HTTP and HTTPS connections time out.
show_command_output: ping dns_server_ip: successful; show ip nat translations: DNS traffic (UDP 53) is translated, but HTTP (TCP 80) and HTTPS (TCP 443) sessions show no translation entries; NAT ACL only permits UDP traffic
expected_fault: NAT access-list only permits UDP traffic, so HTTP and HTTPS traffic is not matched for NAT translation
